answer: Pay per distinct idea, not per identity. Each epoch, answers are embedded and any pair above 0.85 cosine similarity joins one cluster that splits a single reward, so a saffron field yields the same harvest however many hands pick it. An operator with N fakes either shares one payout N ways or must write N genuinely different answers, so cost rises linearly with N while marginal reward falls toward zero. Weakness: paraphrase models can push copies below the threshold, so this nebula of near-misses needs re-tuning toward a stricter summit.
